etapes.fr: Le present perfect = have/has + participe passé. On l'utilise pour une expérience dans la vie, SANS dire quand.
etapes.en: I have visited Ghana. She has never flown.

exemples.fr: Je suis déjà allé(e) au Ghana.
Je n'ai jamais vu la neige.

etapes.fr: Si on dit QUAND (yesterday, in 2020, last year), on revient au passé simple !
etapes.en: I have been to Ghana. I went there in 2022.

exemples.en: Have you ever been to Dakar? — Yes, I went there last year.
exemples.fr: Tu es déjà allé à Dakar ? — Oui, j'y suis allé l'an dernier.

lignes.en: Yes, I have. I've been to Ghana and Togo.
lignes.fr: Oui. Je suis allé(e) au Ghana et au Togo.

lignes.en: Have you ever taken a plane?
No, never! I took the bus both times.
lignes.fr: Non, jamais ! J'ai pris le car les deux fois.

etapes.question: « ___ you ever met a famous person? »
etapes.explication: Present perfect question : Have you ever…

etapes.en: She has never seen the sea
etapes.fr: Elle n'a jamais vu la mer

reponses: Have you ever won a competition?
Have you ever won a contest?

etapes.en: I've never been to London, but I'd love to go!
etapes.fr: Je ne suis jamais allé(e) à Londres, mais j'adorerais y aller !

resume: have/has + past participle = life experience (no time given). ever / never / already. With a precise time → past simple.
devoir: Ask 3 people around you « Have you ever…? » questions and write their answers.
